Article Title: A guiding light: Teacher by title, master of many roles for students
Article Text:
Teachers fulfill diverse roles beyond academic instruction in schools (AI-generated image used for representational purposes)

The many hats Teachers wear





NEW DELHI: Long after the school bell rings, a teacher’s work is rarely done.Between guiding lessons and grading assignments, many are resolving conflicts, counselling distressed children, leading safety committees, overseeing transport routes, organising cultural events and often routinely shouldering responsibilities that stretch well beyond academics.For Sonia Chhabra of Bal Bharati Public School, Pitampura, one such role was that of a “nurturer”.She recalls a Class XI student with a stammer who struggled with confidence. When the school decided to stage Doctor Faustus, she entrusted him with a substantial role.The decision surprised some teachers and students, but Chhabra believed his difficulty stemmed largely from a lack of confidence rather than ability.For nearly a month, she worked closely with him during rehearsals, encouraging and reassuring him.“Then came the final performance. The student walked onto the stage, delivered his role and did not stammer even once. The applause that followed was not merely for his performance. It was for the child who had overcome the fear within him,” she said, adding, “Sometimes, the greatest gift a teacher can give a child is not knowledge, but belief.” Pallavi Sharma , principal of Mamta Modern School, said teachers play multiple roles in schools, balancing committee responsibilities, student welfare, extracurricular activities and administrative duties alongside teaching.Some responsibilities are visible, such as assemblies and cultural programmes. Others, including child welfare and individual mentoring, often remain behind the scenes.One educator recalled helping a Class IV girl who had become withdrawn after losing her mother and adjusting to changes in her family.The teacher regularly spent time counselling her during lunch breaks, gradually helping her open up.Teachers say such experiences highlight an important part of their work: recognising the child behind the student.Balancing these roles can also be demanding.A private school teacher said the challenge was often finding enough time to do justice to multiple responsibilities.“You are teaching and planning lessons, but at the same time you may be handling a committee responsibility, preparing children for an event or dealing with a student who needs your attention. Sometimes the roles overlap throughout the day,” the teacher said.For many educators, however, these responsibilities are inseparable from teaching itself.As Chhabra puts it, teachers often become ‘nurturers’, ‘guides’, ‘listeners, counsellors, motivators’ and even ‘parents away from home’. “The confidence we give a child often stays with them for a lifetime,” she said.
Article Summary: Teachers often become ‘nurturers’, ‘guides’ and ‘listeners, counsellors, motivators’ Pallavi Sharma, principal of Mamta Modern School, said teachers play multiple roles in schools.

Article Title: After triple talaq ban, men use Qazis’ ‘services’ to end nikah
Article Text: Recently, the deputy charity commissioner of Mumbai deregistered Mohakkama-E-Sharia Darul Quza Rehmaniya, a Jogeshwari-based Public Trust which functioned as a sharia court. Faske Nikah or dissolution or annulment of the marriage was among the “several illegal activities” the trust was found to be involved in.This significant order came following Crawford Market resident Rizwana Afzal Shaikh complained to the charity commissioner that the trust, run by Maulana Abdul Hassain Rahi Kazi and a few others, wanted to dissolve her marriage through talaq-e-ahsan, one of the forms of divorce under Islamic law in which the husband pronounces talaq or divorce just once. In this form, the husband can revoke the divorce any time during the iddat period lasting three lunar months. The divorce becomes irrevocable only after the iddat period ends without any reconciliation. Under Muslim Personal Law, this is recognized as a valid form of divorce since triple talaq or talaq-e-biddat (pronouncing triple talaq in one sitting) is illegal, void and criminalized in the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriages) Act, 2019.Shaikh, who married Vile Parle resident Afzal Shaikh in 2005, and they have two children alleged that she was “driven” out of home in December 2020. Subsequently she received a notice from the Trust telling her that her husband wants to give divorce through talaq-e-ahsan. She says she ignored this notice and, after 15 days, she received another notice which she replied to and personally visited the Trust’s office.“I do not want a divorce as I have spent nearly two decades with my husband, and we have two children who live with their father. Where will I go as I have no one except my old mother to turn to,“ said Shaikh.After the mediation efforts failed, two cases, in family court for “restitution of the conjugal rights, and Bandra magistrate court under section 498A alleging cruelty and domestic violence, were filed.In the backdrop of deregistration of the Trust for allegedly carrying out illegal activities, including dissolution of the marriages, approaching Qazis for extra-judicial dissolution of marriage has assumed a menacing proportion. There are many self-appointed Qazis who deliver “swift order” for a fee. Since men are afraid to pronounce triple talaq as it is now criminalised, they are increasingly using the “services” of these “extra-judicial courts” to end their marriage.“Women like Rizwana have no other option but to approach courts to get justice. She says her marriage is still valid and wants to return to her husband’s house,” says Advocate Farhana Shah who represents Shaikh.Since the triple talaq was made illegal, the dissolution of the marriage through sharia courts’ interventions has become an “alternative route”, say many Qazis in the city.Mufti Faiyaz Alam Qasmi, a Muslim-Personal Law Board-appointed Qazi says that he worked from Nagpada for 13 years (2013 to 2026) before he recently moved to Malad.“In the last 13 years, we received around 2500 cases, mostly by women seeking khula (dissolution of marriage). I think most women are seeking khula because of harassment. No Qazi has courage to dissolve a marriage through triple talaq today,” says Qasmi. He adds that the shariah courts are still the better option.Noorjahan Safia Niaz, co-founder of Bhartiya Muslim Mahila Andolan, a co-petitioner in the instant triple talaq case in the Supreme Court, says that men are increaasingly approaching shariah courts.“The anti-triple talaq law is not the final solution. Unless Muslim Personal laws are codified, men will always find a way to harass women with talaq even if it is not triple talaq,” says Niaz.Educationist and businessman Nasir Jamal who is disturnbed at this “mess” observes: “Many Qazis have opened their dukan or shops and need to be educated properly on the rights of women are not inferior to men. Talaq is an option, not a license or a weapon to harass women with.”
Article Summary: Mohakkama-E-Sharia Darul Quza Rehmaniya, a Jogeshwari-based Public Trust which functioned as a sharia court, was deregistered. Rizwana Afzal Shaikh complained to the charity commissioner that the trust wanted to dissolve her marriage through talaq-e-ahsan, one of the forms of divorce under Islamic law.

Article Title: Youth Falls 1,500 Feet at Matheran Hills, Body Recovered After 11 Hours
Article Text: Navi Mumbai: A 21-year-old youth, a house painter, residing in Ambernath, who had gone to the Matheran hills for a monsoon picnic with his friend, died after falling into the gorge at Alexander Point’s cliffside view on Friday around 3.30 pm. His body was retrieved from the gorge at about 1500 feet after an 11-hour search operation. Prima facie, Matheran police have registered an accidental death report.Sarita Musale, senior inspector of Matheran, said that the deceased youth was identified as Sonu Gautam. His friend, who is also a house painter and was accompanying him, said that while he was talking on the mobile at some distance at Alexander Point, Gautam was viewing nature’s beauty by standing close to the cliff. Within two minutes, as his friend turned around, he saw Gautam falling off the cliff into the gorge. His friend informed the Matheran police and showed the spot from which Gautam had fallen into the gorge or else it would have been difficult to trace his body.Inspector Musale said, “To retrieve the body of Gautam from the deep gorge, the members of the professional Matheran Sahayadri Rescue Team were summoned. The rescuers climbed down the gorge using ropes and harness belts. The heavy rains created obstacles in the search operation that lasted for around 11 hours, after which the rescuers spotted Gautam’s body at about 1500 feet in the gorge and carried the body to the top of the hill. Gautam’s body was handed over to his kin, who have not suspected any foul play and hence have not lodged any complaint.
Article Summary: House painter Sonu Gautam, 21, died after falling into the gorge at Alexander Point’s cliffside view on Friday around 3.30 pm. His friend, who is also a house painter and was accompanying him, said that while he was talking on the mobile at some distance at the cliff. Within two minutes, as his friend turned around, he saw Gautsam falling off the cliff into the Gorge. The rescuers climbed down the gorge using ropes and harness belts.

Article Title: ‘Give gold, money for auto’: Former wrestler, 2 kids die after jumping from fort in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Ashwini Pol (L) and Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Wrestler won 5 gold, 6 silver medals: Police

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the accomplishments of individuals in sports can overshadow personal issues they face? Yes, often No, they should be addressed equally 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With inputs from Tushar Dutt in Pune)





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Former national-level wrestler Ashwini Pol (30) and two of her three children died after they jumped from Naldurg fort in Dharashiv district on Thursday.Ashwini’s other daughter, who was seriously injured after the fall, was admitted to a hospital.A case of abetment to suicide and dowry harassment was registered against her husband and in-laws following a complaint by Ashwini’s father, Tanaji Shivaji Mohite (54), a teacher from Whantal in Umarga, police said on Friday.Ravindra Gaikwad, investigating officer in the case, said, “Ashwini’s husband, father- and mother-in-law, and aunt, all residents of Ambulga in Latur district’s Nilanga taluka, allegedly used to harass her by saying that her parents had not given anything in dowry. Ashwini was also subjected to mental torture after she gave birth to twins.” One of the twins died in the tragedy.Police said her husband and in-laws would pressure her to get her parents to give gold bangles and money to buy an auto. “Fed up with the harassment, she jumped off Naldurg fort along with her three children,” an officer said.Ashwini was a wrestler from Marathwada and had won five gold and six silver medals in state- and national-level competitions, police said. “She was a promising wrestler and had won medals,” former wrestler, coach and international referee Dinesh Gund said.No one was arrested at the time of going to press.
Article Summary: Former national-level wrestler Ashwini Pol (30) and two of her three children died after they jumped from Naldurg fort in Dharashiv district on Thursday. A case of abetment to suicide and dowry harassment was registered against her husband and in-laws.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.

Article Title: 12-year-old girl, young woman rescued from prostitution racket in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Cops can be seen walking with 2 women. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued a 12-year-old girl and a 26-year-old woman from a prostitution racket being carried out at a lodge in Nerul after conducting a raid by sending a decoy customer on Thursday.The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers by providing them rooms at Kohinoor Palace Lodging and Boarding in Shiravane village, Nerul.Gajanan Kadam, AHTU senior inspector, said the rescued minor girl hails from UP and resided in Shiravane village with her cousins, who had brought her from UP after telling her parents that she would be given a job.The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours after booking a room. The accused demanded Rs 4,000 for supplying a woman.After the accused accepted the amount, the decoy customer signalled the police team waiting outside the lodge, following which they raided the premises.Inspector Kadam said, “The arrested accused are the lodge managers identified as Hridaykumar Singh and Deepak Ramrakhiani and the waiter Kuleshwar Kumar Singh.”At Nerul police station, an FIR was registered against the arrested accused by invoking BNS sections for trafficking of persons and joint criminal liability, along with the POCSO Act, which defines punishment for abetment, such as helping, encouraging or plotting any sexual crime against a child, and the Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act.On Friday, the three accused were produced before the Belapur JMFC court, which remanded them to police custody till Sept 9.
Article Summary: The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers. The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours.

Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Teen murdered, body dumped near Mini Seashore
Article Text:
A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi





NAVI MUMBAI: A 19-year-old boy was murdered and his body was dumped on the pavement near a public garden along Mini Seashore Road in Sector 10A, Vashi, early on Saturday morning. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused.Shashikant Chandekar, senior inspector of Vashi police station, said, "The murder victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane. A passing pedestrian spotted him lying unconscious in a pool of blood on the pavement around 4am. The pedestrian alerted Vashi police station, and our police team reached the spot and took the teenager to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead due to severe blood loss from grievous injuries to his head and wrist after being assaulted with some sharp lethal weapon. The victim Mahato hails from Bihar and resided with his father, who is an auto-rickshaw driver, his mother and two minor siblings. He worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and used to drive his father's auto-rickshaw during the night."Inspector Chandekar added, "Mahato had left home on Friday around 9pm, telling his mother that he was going to work at the Chinese food stall and was taking his father's auto-rickshaw to ferry passengers throughout the night.After his body was found early on Saturday morning, his family was informed. His father's auto-rickshaw was not found at the crime scene. Hence, it is suspected that after fatally assaulting Mahato, the assailant took away the auto-rickshaw, which is being traced by scanning CCTV footage along the route from Koparkhairane to Vashi."As there is no CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we are scanning CCTV footage from roads leading to the crime spot where Mahato's body was dumped to zero in on the suspect. Mahato might have been fatally assaulted at the spot, or he might have been assaulted at another location and his body brought in a vehicle and dumped near Mini Seashore. Accordingly, using technical expertise, efforts are being made to detect the murder case. Meanwhile, Mahato's kin and friends are being questioned to get some lead on the unidentified accused."
Article Summary: A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused. The victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane.

Article Title: 3 youths treckking to Chanderi fort near Panvel miss way, get stranded; rescued by cops
Article Text:
The rescued youths aged 22-25 years were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan.





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way and got stranded before being rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday.Gajanan Ghadge, Senior Inspector of Panvel Taluka Police Station, said that the rescued youths, aged between 22 and 25 years, were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan. They had started their trek at around 8 am.At around 11 am, the police helpline number 112 received a distress call from one of the trekkers, informing officials that they had lost their way while trekking towards Chanderi Fort."Upon receiving the information, we contacted the caller and asked him to share his live Google location. Accordingly, our police team, along with the Wavanje check-post beat marshal, Ritghar village head Deepak Patil, and the rescue team of NGO Sahyadri Pratishthan, launched a search operation by tracking the youth's mobile location," Ghadge said.The three youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.
Article Summary: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way. They were rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday. The youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai road rage: Ola driver attacked with stick, dragged 2km on car bonnet
Article Text:
The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a road rage incident in Nerul after an argument between the drivers of an Ola cab and a Swift car as the latter claimed that the Ola cab driver had dangerously cut his way while overtaking on the internal road in Nerul on August 15 night, the Swift car driver assaulted the cab driver by punching on his nose and hitting on the head with a bamboo stick causing him severe injuries.As the cab driver bled profusely and attempted to stop the car driver from getting away till the cops arrived, by lying on the car's bonnet, the car driver drove with the cab driver on the bonnet for about 2 kms.The cab driver while recording the incident on his mobile in one hand and firmly holding the bonnet by other hand, shouted for help from passing motorists, while dangling dangerously and requesting the car driver to stop by yelling that he could fall and get killed.As the car slowed down after some distance, the cab driver jumped off the bonnet after which the car driver sped away leaving the cab driver injured on the road.The incident occured on the stretch in sector 20 near Nerul pond on August 15 around 9.35pm.Ajay Kamble, senior inspector of Nerul said, "As per the complaint by the injured cab driver identified as Pradeepkumar Pandey, 27, a resident of Naigaon (E), an FIR was registered at Nerul police station against the unidentified accused car driver, who is absconding.From the Swift car's registration number provided by the complainant, the accused driver was identified as Lalit Arjun Patil, a resident of Juinagar. ""We have invoked relevant BNS sections for the offences of voluntarily causing hurt/ grievous hurt using dangerous weapons or means, voluntarily causing simple hurt, rash or negligent driving on a public way in a manner that endangers human life or is likely to cause hurt or injury to any person and causing simple hurt to any person through a rash or negligent act that endangers human life or personal safety," inspector Kamble added.As per the FIR, on August 15 at 8.18pm, the complainant Pandey had picked up two women passengers from Andheri and dropped them at Seawoods Grand Central mall in Nerul at around 9.30pm.Thereafter, he headed towards Sarsole to attend birthday party of his cousin Nitin Pandey's brother-in-law Rahul Chaubey.Around 9.35pm, when he reached near Nerul pond in sector 20, suddenly a Swift car driver was repeatedly honking. Hence, he changed the lane and gave him way to go ahead.But, the car driver waylaid him and alighting from his car claimed that he had dangerously cut his way while overtaking and punched on his nose, while hurling expletives.As the complainant tried to convince him and told not to give bad words, the car driver went to his vehicle and taking out a bamboo stick, hit on his head causing severe bleeding.As the assailant sat in his car, the complainant tried to stop him, but he started his car. Hence, the complainant lied on the car's bonnet to prevent him from escaping till the cops arrived.The assailant drove with the complainant on the bonnet for about 2kms, reluctant to stop the car.After some distance, as the car slowed down, he jumped off the bonnet and the assailant sped away.The complainant returned to his cab and called his cousin Dipanshu Pandey, who took him to NMMC's Meenatai Thackeray hospital, Nerul.The doctors gave him first aid and for further treatment referred him to NMMC hospital in Vashi, where he was administered sutures to head injury, followed by CT scan.Thereafter, he lodged a police complaint.
Article Summary: The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm. The Swift car driver assaulted the cab driver by punching on his nose and hitting on the head with a bamboo stick causing him severe injuries. The cab driver attempted to stop the car driver from getting away till the cops arrived, by lying on the car's bonnet.
